svg.text: PRINCIPLES 10 – 13 · DATA, SUPPLY CHAIN, ESCALATION, TELEMETRY

g.text: P10 · AI DATA-AT-REST IS A GOVERNED SURFACE
AI features accrete state: prompt snapshots, raw
responses, reasoning text, vectors, feedback ledgers.
Each is capped (100k-char snapshot limits), gated
where sensitive (reasoning storage opt-out), and
recorded in the security assessment when introduced.
Embeddings are regenerable derived data — drop freely.
P11 · THE MODEL IS PART OF THE SUPPLY CHAIN
Weights enter through the offline channel: pinned,
checksummed, in the SBOM, scanned.
Proven live: the dependency-audit gate caught a
malicious release of a core web framework. A
poisoned GGUF is harder to spot than a poisoned
wheel — provenance matters more, not less.
P12 · LOW CONFIDENCE ESCALATES TO A HUMAN
Verdicts carry numeric confidence; per-alert-type
thresholds decide surface vs suppress. Below the bar,
the analyst sees an explicit "auto-escalated" state —
the AI standing down, not a low-quality guess.
A circuit breaker halts sustained low-confidence output.
Thresholds tuned from ledger data, not intuition.
P13 · OBSERVABILITY WITHOUT EGRESS
AI ops monitoring (latency, tokens, failure rates,
loop health) is first-party and opt-in — exported only
to collectors the operator owns, inside the estate.
Default OFF. Enabling it is a deliberate, documented
deployment decision.
Model selection note: chain-of-thought variants were rejected for free-text surfaces (reasoning leakage).
